content.introduction: Inflation in the United States is measured by the Consumer Price Index, showing annual percentage changes in the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services. The key series is CPIAUCSL from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The latest data is available on the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis's FRED platform.
body: U.S. financial, economic, and banking history. Home > Categories > International Data > Countries > United States. # Inflation, consumer prices for the United States (FPCPITOTLZGUSA). Inflation as measured by the consumer price index reflects the annual percentage change in the cost to the average consumer of acquiring a basket of goods and services that may be fixed or changed at specified intervals, such as yearly.
